This First-Ever Double Decker Park Tiny Is an Absolute Dream
20 photos
Photo: Park Model Homes
A rose by any other name might smell just as sweet in Shakespeare's world, but with a park tiny, the packaging does a lot of heavy lifting. If you look at the newest Woodland Park Liberty model, you might even say the packaging is everything.
The Liberty, or the Timber Ridge RL-260L by its full name, is one of the most popular floorplans from U.S.-based park tiny manufacturer Woodland Park. It's designed to offer sleeping for as many as eight people and to include all the creature comforts of a traditional home, except it sits on a quad-axle oversize trailer.
As such, it's the perfect vacation lodge, wherever you decide (and are allowed) to park it. For 2027, it will be even "more perfect," thanks to a series of upgrades and add-ons that help it live like a brand new floorplan. As such, Woodland Park is also giving it a new name, calling it the Double Decker TR-260L.
One dealer is even going as far as to call it the first-ever double decker park tiny . Don't take that in an absolute sense, because there definitely are other units out there that feature an exterior double porch. But this IS the first model of its kind from Woodland Park, so claims of being the "first" aren't misleading.
Photo: Park Model Homes Like the original model, this park tiny sits on a quad-axle trailer and comes in at 36 feet (11 meters) of length and 11 feet (3.3 meters) of width, but overall length is 46 feet (14 meters) with the double 10-foot (3-meter) porch, aka the highlight of the unit. That also means that you get a double entry, through the porch and through the middle of the home.
Modifications for 2027 are more of the "upgrading" kind. The sliding double glass door that served as the main entry in the original model is now replaced by a wide but fully residential door, and the glass doors are moved onto the porch. The bedroom is still on a dropped frame construction, but it's been completely redesigned. The same for the bathroom.
You still have ample sleeping space , with as high a capacity as eight people if you also make use of the sleeper sofa in the living room and the two double mattresses in the loft. You still have a chef's kitchen with a J-bar counter that's both a breakfast bar and prep surface, a fully dry bathroom, and a main bedroom on the ground floor.
Photo: Park Model Homes In many ways, this is still the same popular floorplan, but now offered with a more entertainment-friendly features.
The two decks, for instance, are perfect for that. You can host outdoor parties or use them as personal outdoor lounges by adding patio furniture, and the upper one offers a complete bird's eye view of of whatever area you're parked at.
Unlike with other park models, you don't get a TV on either deck or stuff like fireplaces or even full outdoor kitchens. But the simple possibility of taking your meals or your parties outside, while still be close enough to your home, is a nice bonus .
Photo: Park Model Homes The layout is the same as in the previous years, with the living room at one end and the bedroom at the other. The oversize loft, now offered with black safety rails and a floating steps, spreads out over the entire bedroom and the bathroom.
Since the bedroom is on a dropped frame, you get more headroom in the corresponding section of the loft. In other words, you have two levels inside the loft, which allows you to have two double beds in there with some semblance of separation, if not actual privacy.
The first unit completed and shown in the second video at the bottom of the page shows the loft with a second smart TV, a window-mounted AC, carpeted floors, and still plenty of space to move around.
Photo: Park Model Homes The bedroom under the loft has been redesigned altogether. Woodland Park changes the disposition of the queen bed to make room for a walk-in wardrobe behind a bar door for 2027, while still offering matching nightstands, a full storage compartment under the bed, and overhead cabinetry. The wardrobe is equipped with a bank of drawers, shelves, hanging space, and even a small frosted window.
The bathroom is seeing a share of changes as well, from the new surround in the shower to the upgraded linen closet by the vanity. Being a park tiny and, as such, designed to stay parked on location, where it will be hooked up to utilities, it comes with a residential plumbed toilet.
The kitchen and open-plan living room remain unchanged though. For 2027, this park tiny is equipped with stainless steel residential appliances, laminate counters, and shaker cabinets in a new color choice. It also offers plenty of space for moving around and entertaining.
Photo: Park Model Homes Past the breakfast bar is the large living room, offered standard with a sleeper sofa and an entertainment wall with a WiFi-connected 3D fireplace and a smart TV over a wood mantle. The forward part of the trailer, so the spaces in the living and kitchen, have extra ceiling height and lots of natural light thanks to lots of glazing, including clerestory windows.
The Double Decker TR-26L offers 396 square feet (36.7 square meters) of living space across the ground-level floor, to which you add the loft and the two decks, which aren't taken into account.
The unit shown below is selling for $149,898 with everything included.
